meta.title: Working with Intelligaia
meta.lede: Answers to the questions clients most often ask before starting an engagement. This is a sample document.

blocks.question: What does Intelligaia do?
blocks.answer: Intelligaia is a product design and engineering partner that helps enterprises put AI to work in real interfaces. We cover UX research, design strategy, design systems, and delivery — the path from understanding a user's problem to a shipped, accessible product.

blocks.question: How does an engagement usually start?
blocks.answer: With the problem, not a deliverable. We run a short discovery to establish who the user is, what outcome you need, and what's blocking it today. Only then do we scope the work — so the first thing you get is a shared, evidence-based view of the problem, not a guess at a solution.

blocks.question: Do we need to have everything figured out before we talk to you?
blocks.answer: No. A lot of our work starts from an ambiguous brief. Bringing us in early — while the problem is still fuzzy — usually saves time, because the framing is where the expensive mistakes are avoided.

blocks.question: How do you work with our internal team?
blocks.answer:
As one team, not a vendor over the wall. We work in your tools where it makes sense, share progress continuously rather than in big reveals, and leave your team more capable at the end than at the start.
Where a design system is involved, we build so your team can maintain it after we're gone.

blocks.question: What tools do you design in?
blocks.answer: Primarily Figma — auto-layout, variables, and component libraries — so what we hand over is a living system, not flat mockups. Research, strategy, and delivery artifacts come in whatever format your team already works in.

blocks.question: How do you handle accessibility?
blocks.answer: WCAG 2.1 AA is a requirement from the first frame, not a final audit. Contrast, focus order, target size, and screen-reader behavior are part of the brief, and every core view is designed for its full range of states — empty, loading, error, first-use, and power-user.

blocks.question: How long does a typical engagement take?
blocks.answer: It depends on scope, but most focused engagements run in phases — a short discovery, then design and delivery in increments you can review as they land, rather than one long stretch with a reveal at the end. [TK: typical engagement length for this service]

blocks.answer: [TK: pricing model — fixed-scope vs. time-and-materials, and payment schedule]. We'll always tie the commercials to a clearly scoped set of outcomes so you know what you're buying.

blocks.question: What do we get at handoff?
blocks.answer: Build-ready design: a Figma file with auto-layout and variables, documented component states, accessibility notes, and the rationale behind the key decisions — everything your engineers need to build without guessing, and everything your team needs to maintain it afterward.
